name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent
operator: GitHub (the vendor); each organisation is the operator of its own deployment
what: The asynchronous agent on GitHub.com that creates branches, writes code and opens pull requests in response to assigned issues.
note: An example scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar; the closest published shape, a hosted Actions runner with no agent, is not the same thing.

I04.n: It writes code in an "ephemeral, firewalled environment".

I08.n: It "can create branches, write code, and open pull requests in response to assigned issues".

I10.n: It can take information and context from MCP and from external applications such as Microsoft Teams, Linear, Slack and Jira.
I10.span: external applications like Microsoft Teams, Linear, Slack, and Jira

I11.n: Repository-level MCP servers connect it to external tools; by default only the GitHub server (read-only token on the current repository) and a Playwright server limited to localhost are configured.
I11.span: GitHub.com supports MCP servers configured at the repository level

I18.n: It creates branches, writes code and opens pull requests on its own; the page says to review and test its output before merging.
I18.span: always review and test the content generated by the cloud agent

I20.n: The vendor states intended uses: maintenance, feature development, prototyping.

I21.n: "It can only push to a single branch"; it has no access to Actions secrets beyond those configured for it.
I21.span: It can only push to a single branch

I22.n: The page lists limitations: limited scope, inaccurate code, security risks, public code matches.

I25.n: Read-only where the user has only read access; one branch to push to.

I27.n: Its commits are signed and show as Verified.

I38.n: Workflows triggered by its pull requests "require approval from a user with write access before they will run".
I38.span: require approval from a user with write access before they will run

I41.n: Each commit message links to the agent session logs, and its commits are authored by Copilot with the person as co-author.
I41.span: Each commit message includes a link to the agent session logs

I56.n: Its commits are authored by Copilot, with the person who started the task marked as co-author.
I56.span: authored by Copilot, with the human who started the task marked as the co-author

S2.n: A registry lists servers that partners and the community publish for it.
S2.span: a curated list of MCP servers from partners and the community

S3.n: The documentation publishes an llms.txt index.

not_credited.what: New code is analysed with CodeQL, secret scanning and dependency analysis during generation.
not_credited.why: That tests what the agent produces. No indicator asks for it yet, and it is not evidence that the agent itself is tested.

configurations.name: As shipped
configurations.note: The firewall and its recommended allowlist are on.

configurations.name: With external tools connected
configurations.note: Model Context Protocol servers and other applications.

moved: As above. Scanning of generated code is no longer counted as testing of the agent.

findings.finding: The mode may be wrong. The MCP page says "The GitHub MCP server and Playwright MCP server are configured by default" for the cloud agent. The answer marks I11 available with an mcp configuration and the "As shipped" configuration leaves it out. Decide from the source whether connecting to external services is the default, and fix the mode or say why not.

The span "provided and maintained by GitHub" is in the source, but the indicator is a published protocol between agents. MCP, as the page describes it, connects an agent to tools and context, not agent to agent. This is credited to the wrong indicator. Remove, or cite a page that describes agent-to-agent communication.

"Across one organisation" comes from the sentence that the agent is "constrained to data across a single organization in Chat mode". That is a limit, in one mode, not a statement that it works across several systems. The credit needs a sentence about breadth (repositories, issues, pull requests, external applications). The responsible-use page has the external-integrations sentence naming Teams, Linear, Slack and Jira; consider citing that.

The note cites the co-author line and the public-code matches. The page says more directly "Each commit message includes a link to the agent session logs". Cite that sentence: it is what covers what the agent does. The indicator needs the operation, so documented will not count; the note should still be right about what supports it.

Commits and pull requests attributed to Copilot is true ("authored by Copilot, with the human who started the task marked as the co-author") but is not the agent telling the people it talks to that it is an AI. Weak credit; consider whether it stands.
Both quotations are in the firewall page (12 and 8 words). The scope says a measured grant only, and this scan has none. The answer is accurate; the scorer should not count it as holding. Check.
The note says the person reviews the pull request before merging. I could not find that sentence in the responsible-use page. Cite the sentence or soften the note.

The span "It can only push to a single branch" (8 words) is in the page. The second half, no access to Actions secrets beyond those configured for it, is the page's: "only secrets and variables specifically added to the copilot environment are passed to the agent". Correct.
The span is in the page and is 12 words. The sentence is about workflows run by its pull requests, which is a real approval gate on a high-impact action.
The span "a curated list of MCP servers from partners and the community" is in the page. 11 words.

Opened each source. I27: the page says the commits are signed and appear as "Verified". I08 quotes 14 words, under the limit. I22 lists limited scope, inaccurate code, security risks, matches with public code, all on the page.

review.note: Published as an example on 10 November 2026, before the review workflow existed. Mapped by one agent. It goes through two rounds of review next.

responses.response: Mode kept as available, re-sourced to the MCP page: the two servers configured by default are GitHub’s own, with a read-only token on the current repository, and Playwright, limited to localhost, so neither crosses a trust boundary; external servers are added per repository.

Removed. MCP connects the agent to tools, not agent to agent; the page’s Agent finder implements a discovery specification for capabilities, not a communication layer between agents. Reach falls from level three to two and the open-protocol badge goes.

Replaced with the external-integrations sentence naming Teams, Linear, Slack and Jira (span verified), marked available under the mcp configuration since those integrations are set up per organisation.
Note now cites the sentence that each commit message links to the agent session logs (span verified). It stays documented, so as an operation fact it does not count.

Kept with the page’s own sentence as span: commits authored by Copilot tell reviewers of its work that an AI wrote them, read under aiact.art-50, which also covers marking AI output. Round two may still judge it.
Removed. The scope reads I45 from a measured grant only and this scan has none; the firewall sentences remain true but cannot carry it.

Note softened to what the page says: it works on its own to a pull request, and the page advises reviewing and testing before merging (span verified). No sentence says the person must review before merge.
